title: Tiered availability contracts, progressive throttling gates, and per-tenant error budgets
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Define and codify tiered availability contracts (Gold/Silver/Bronze) with deterministic latency bands, per-tenant error budget accounting, and progressive throttling/rollback gates for staged rollouts of runtime changes. Deliver acceptance criteria, monitoring dashboards, and an automated gate implementation that can be reused by future releases.
acceptance_criteria: Three contract tiers defined with explicit SLOs: Gold (99.95% availability, p50<=25ms, p95<=120ms, p99<=350ms), Silver (99.9% availability, p50<=40ms, p95<=200ms, p99<=500ms), Bronze (99.5% availability, p50<=70ms, p95<=350ms, p99<=800ms)
Per-tenant error budgets calculated hourly and rolled up daily; system exposes remaining budget as a metric (tenant.error_budget.remaining) and flags when burn rate exceeds 2x over a 1-hour window

Rollout gating policy implemented: canary (1% traffic, 30m), ramp to 10% (60m), ramp to 50% (120m) with automated checks; any gate fails when availability drops below tier target or p95 latency increases >30% relative to baseline

Automated gate evaluation runs against production-grade synthetic and real traffic signals: latency percentiles, 5xx rate, tail latencies, and queue length; implementation is configurable per release and per tenant tier
Alerting and dashboards created: per-tenant SLO dashboard, error-budget burn-rate alert, rollout health view in Console; links documented and visible to on-call and product owners
Rollbacks automated: if gate fails at any stage, traffic re-routes to previous stable model/runtime variant and incident runbook is paged with root-cause triage checklist
Performance test harness (load + KV cache patterns) executed for each candidate runtime change with results stored in CI artifacts and linked to the release ticket
Acceptance tests for per-tenant billing and quota behavior to ensure throttles do not incorrectly affect invoicing or rate-limited tenants
Documentation: PRD, rollout policy, and runbook published in Confluence; SDK and API docs updated for new telemetry metric names and gating API
notes: Trade-off: stricter Gold SLOs raise capacity costs—proposal includes autoscaling policy recommendations and cost-estimates for customers to opt into tiers
Decision: use burn-rate gating strategy (derived from error-budget framework) instead of absolute 5xx thresholds to better reflect latency-driven regressions
Follow-up: engineering to prototype gate evaluation as a reusable library (ENG-40321); Console team to add rollout health panel (ENG-40901)
Early customer ask: large fintech tenant requested Gold SLA with dedicated KV caching; add as optional capability in Dedicated offering
rollout_plan: Stage 0 — Canary: 1% traffic, evaluation window 30 minutes, must pass all gate checks to continue
Stage 1 — Small Ramp: 10% traffic, evaluation window 60 minutes, stop if error_budget.remaining < 20% or p95 > baseline*1.3
Stage 2 — Medium Ramp: 50% traffic, evaluation window 120 minutes, stop if availability below tier SLA or sustained 5xx rate > 0.1%
Stage 3 — Global: 100% traffic; final verification 24h post-rollout with daily burn rate checks for 7 days
Manual hold points at each stage for high-impact tenants (Gold) where product owner must sign off before progressing
Fallback: automatic rollback to previous runtime variant and notification to on-call and release owner on gate fail
runbook: On-call checklist: page on how to triage increased p95 latency including KV cache warmup, kernel scheduling regressions, and autoscaler lag
Rollback playbook: automated re-route + retrospective template + customer communications template
observability: Synthetic probe: global regional probes hitting representative endpoints every 30s
Tracing: sample 1% traces for high-volume tenants and 10% for canaries
qa_tests: Load test scenario simulating mixed chat and embeddings workload with KV cache hit ratios matching production
Chaos experiment: introduce transient GPU node loss during canary and verify gate catches degradation
Tenant isolation test: simulate noisy neighbor and ensure Gold tenant SLO remains within target under isolation settings
Billing/quotas test: verify throttle-induced errors return correct error codes and do not bill extra tokens
